 Live updates: Broward and Miami-Dade public schools to remain closed Thursday due to flooding 
 Find live updates of the latest breaking news across South Florida. 
 By Briana Trujillo , Adam Berg and NBC6 • 
 Published November 18, 2026 • 
 Updated 15 minutes ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 The NBC6 South Florida News streaming channel plays local South Florida news 24 hours a day, seven days a week. 
 What to Know
 A flood watch remains in effect on Wednesday for much of South Florida after storms dumped several inches of rain over the region—more than a foot in some spots—on Tuesday and Tuesday night along with hail up to one inch, about the size of a quarter. 
 Broward County Public Schools are closed and will remain closed Thursday. Broward County declared a local state of emergency. 
 Miami-Dade County Public Schools will also close Thursday, NBC6 confirmed.
 Several cities in South Florida are feeling the impacts. Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood have issued their own emergency alerts. Miami Beach and Hollywood are waiving fees at city-owned parking garages for residents. 
 A temporary ground stop has been lifted at Miami International Airport (MIA) and Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL).
 Scattered showers and thunderstorms are still expected for Thursday, but better conditions Friday and sunshine expected for the weekend.
 Flood damage: What your home and car insurance may cover after heavy rain
 This week's heavy rain has left drivers stranded and some homeowners dealing with flood damage across South Florida.
 Now, many residents are trying to figure out what to do next — and whether their insurance policies will cover the damage.
 Insurance experts say the answer depends on the type of coverage you have and, in some cases, how the damage occurred.
 What to do if your car floods 
 If your vehicle was stranded in floodwater, experts recommend not starting the engine. Instead, have the car towed to a mechanic for an inspection to determine whether it is safe to drive.
 "Because even if the car seems like it's OK, there could be a lot of things lurking under the hood that you might not be aware of that could go out on you," said Mark Jenkins with AAA.
 Jenkins also recommends documenting the damage by taking pictures, which can help when filing an insurance claim.
 But whether your insurance will pay for repairs depends on your policy.
 "People might wonder whether insurance covers flood damage like this, and that really all just depends on whether you have comprehensive coverage. This is an optional coverage, so you want to check your policy to find out if you have it," Jenkins said.
 Even with comprehensive coverage, the circumstances surrounding the flooding may affect whether a claim is approved.
 Mark Friedlander with the Insurance Information Institute, an insurance industry trade group, says there may be a difference between a vehicle damaged by rising floodwater while parked and one driven into a flooded street.
 "So sudden acts are covered... but If you intentionally try to drive through a flooded street or a flooded neighborhood, in most cases, your claims could be denied because that was an intentional act that could have been avoided," Friedlander said.
 Does homeowners’ insurance cover flooding? 
 When it comes to damage to your home, the type of insurance coverage is just as important.
 Standard homeowners’ insurance policies do not cover flooding caused by rising water. That protection generally requires a separate flood insurance policy.
 Friedlander says only one in five homeowners in South Florida have flood insurance.
 "So, most people who are in situations where it's voluntary to purchase flood insurance, they don't buy it," he said.
 While a homeowners insurance policy may cover certain types of damage, such as roof leaks caused by heavy rain, rising floodwater requires separate flood coverage.
 That distinction can make a significant difference for homeowners trying to recover from a storm.
 Why you shouldn't wait until a storm approaches 
 Friedlander also warns that homeowners should not wait until a storm is approaching to purchase flood insurance.
 "So, you can't decide at the last minute when you hear a bad weather forecast that I'm going to go out and buy flood insurance now. It's too late for the upcoming storm but the fact that we expect numerous storms impacting most areas of Florida throughout the winter months due to El Nino, time to prepare is now," Friedlander said.
 The National Flood Insurance Program generally has a  30-day waiting period  before a new policy takes effect, while private insurers may have waiting periods ranging from 15 to 30 days.
 That means purchasing coverage when heavy rain is already in the forecast may be too late to protect against damage from that storm.
 For South Floridians dealing with the aftermath of flooding, experts recommend documenting damage, reviewing insurance policies and understanding what is covered before filing a claim.

 ‘We'll come back stronger than ever': Part of roof at Temple Sinai collapses
 Wind advisory issued for most of South Florida
 The National Weather Service issued a wind advisory for coastal and metro Broward, Miami-Dade and Palm Beach counties.
 It lasts until 1 a.m. Thursday.
 Click here for the latest weather alerts.
 A Wind Advisory has been issued until 1 a.m. on Thursday, November 19.
Residents and visitors are urged to secure outdoor furniture, balcony items and other loose objects that could become airborne. Use extra caution while driving especially on bridges and causeways, and remain mindful of strong wind gusts. Pedestrians should also be aware of their surroundings when outdoors.

 Miami-Dade Schools will be closed tomorrow
 Miami-Dade County Public Schools will be closed tomorrow, NBC6 confirmed.
 The district remained open today.
 Hollywood synagogue roof partially collapses after overnight storms
 The roof of a synagogue in Hollywood partially collapsed as storms hit Broward County overnight.
 The 500-seat Temple Sinai of Hollywood was left in ruins. Images from Chopper6 showed the buckled roof and a huge crack in the wall of the sanctuary.
 "I walked into the sanctuary; I couldn’t go more than two feet," Barry Greenberger said. "Everything was collapsed into the pews."
 As flooding effects Broward County, part of the roof at Temple Sinai in Hollywood collapsed. NBC6's Julia Bagg reports.
 The synagogue has hosted weddings, funerals and holidays for decades.
 “Apparently the rain was so heavy, the rain, the hail, and the winds were very strong, so something extraordinary happened there and the weight just brought it all down," Rabbi Gideon Goldenholz said.
 Some of the most sacred items inside the temple are the Torah scrolls. The rabbi said he and some members were able to safely remove one, which was preserved from the Holocaust. But there are about a dozen other scrolls that they have not been able to reach.
 "We’re a resilient community; we’ll rebuild, we’ll come back stronger than ever. And we’ll do it together. Thank God nobody got hurt; that’s the blessing that we have here," Greenberger said.
